summary: A solicitation from SRI-ARC asking whether network users wanted on-site classes on NLS, the oNLine System, rather than traveling to SRI. It outlines course contents and logistics, and tentatively proposes trips to Washington D.C. in early May and Boston in early June.

plainLanguage.summary: SRI-ARC asks whether network users want NLS classes at their own sites. The RFC outlines the course, room needs, and tentative travel plans.

subtitle: SRI-ARC asks whether network sites want on-site NLS classes.

tldr.problem: Network users had expressed interest in NLS classes at sites other than SRI-ARC.
tldr.mechanism: SRI-ARC solicits interest and outlines a flexible two- to three-day class and the facilities needed.
tldr.outcome: The announcement tentatively considers visits to Washington in May and Boston in June and asks for responses by April 15.

sections.title: Classes at Network Sites
sections.content:
SRI-ARC says users had expressed interest in holding NLS classes at network sites rather than at SRI-ARC. The RFC asks whether a class at or near each recipient's site would be useful.

The authors say they are eager to participate and would value consultation with experienced network users.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI-ARC asks whether users would find local NLS classes useful. The request follows interest in holding classes away from SRI-ARC.

sections.title: Course Outline
sections.content:
The course is described as a comprehensive introduction to using NLS over the network and generally runs for two to three days, depending on participants. Its outline covers basic concepts, entering and using information, and sorting and searching.

The outline is flexible and can be adapted to applications or needs at a particular site.
sections.plainLanguage: The class covers basic NLS use, information handling, and searching. The instructors can adjust the outline for each group's needs.

sections.title: Classroom and Travel Arrangements
sections.content:
Planning information says the preferred class size is six, with an upper limit of ten. The site should provide a room, a teletype-type terminal and network connection for each student, a flip-chart stand, and a large blackboard.

SRI-ARC tentatively considered Washington visits during the first week of May and Boston visits during the first week of June. It asked sites to respond by April 15 and said other arrangements would be considered.
sections.plainLanguage: Each student needs a terminal and connection, and the room needs presentation equipment. The travel dates are tentative, and SRI-ARC asks sites to reply by April 15.
